verses.zh: 「你要用十幅幔子做帐幕。这些幔子要用捻的细麻和蓝色、紫色、朱红色线制造，并用巧匠的手工绣上基路伯。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “The tabernacle itself[NOTE:2] you are to make with[NOTE:3] ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue and purple and scarlet;[NOTE:4] you are to make them with[NOTE:5] cherubim that are the work of an artistic designer.
notes: This chapter is given over to the details of the structure itself, the curtains, coverings, boards and walls and veil. The passage can be studied on one level for its function both practically and symbolically for Israel’s worship. On another level it can be studied for its typology, for the tabernacle and many of its parts speak of Christ. For this one should see the commentaries.

The word order in Hebrew thrusts the direct object to the front for particular emphasis. After the first couple of pieces of furniture are treated (chap. 25), attention turns to the tabernacle itself.
This is for the adverbial accusative explaining how the dwelling place is to be made.
S. R. Driver suggests that the curtains were made with threads dyed with these colors (Exodus, 280). Perhaps the colored threads were used for embroidering the cherubim in the curtains.

The construction is difficult in this line because of the word order. “Cherubim” is an adverbial accusative explaining how they were to make the curtains. And מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב (maʿaseh khoshev) means literally “work of a designer”; it is in apposition to “cherubim.” The Hebrew participle means “designer” or “deviser” so that one could render this “of artistic designs in weaving” (S. R. Driver, Exodus, 280-81). B. Jacob says that it refers to “artistic weavers” (Exodus, 789).

verses.zh: 每幅幔子要长二十八肘，宽四肘，幔子都要一样的尺寸。
verses.en: The length of each[NOTE:1] curtain is to be 42 feet, and the width of each curtain is to be 6 feet[NOTE:2]—the same size for each of the curtains.
notes: Heb “one” (so KJV).
Heb “28 cubits” long and “4 cubits” wide.

verses.zh: 这五幅幔子要幅幅相连；那五幅幔子也要幅幅相连。
verses.en: Five curtains are to be joined,[NOTE:1] one to another,[NOTE:2] and the other[NOTE:3] five curtains are to be joined, one to another.
notes: This is the active participle, not the passive. It would normally be rendered “joining together.” The Bible uses the active because it has the result of the sewing in mind, namely, that every curtain accompanies another (U. Cassuto, Exodus, 348).
Heb “a woman to her sister,” this form of using nouns to express “one to another” is selected because “curtains” is a feminine noun (see GKC 448 §139.e).
The phrase “the other” has been supplied.

verses.zh: 在这相连的幔子末幅边上要做蓝色的钮扣；在那相连的幔子末幅边上也要照样做。
verses.en: You are to make loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in one set, and in the same way you are to make loops[NOTE:1] in the outer edge of the end curtain in the second set.
notes: Here “loops” has been supplied.

verses.zh: 要在这相连的幔子上做五十个钮扣；在那相连的幔子上也做五十个钮扣，都要两两相对。
verses.en: You are to make 50 loops on the one curtain, and you are to make 50 loops on the end curtain which is on the second set, so that the loops are opposite one to another.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “a woman to her sister.”

verses.zh: 又要做五十个金钩，用钩使幔子相连，这才成了一个帐幕。
verses.en: You are to make 50 gold clasps and join the curtains together with the clasps, so that the tabernacle is a unit.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “one”; KJV “it shall be one tabernacle”; NRSV “that the tabernacle may be one whole”; NLT “a single unit.”

verses.zh: 「你要用山羊毛织十一幅幔子，作为帐幕以上的罩棚。
verses.en: “You are to make curtains of goats’ hair[NOTE:1] for a tent over the tabernacle;[NOTE:2] you are to make[NOTE:3] 11 curtains.
notes: This chapter will show that there were two sets of curtains and two sets of coverings that went over the wood building to make the tabernacle or dwelling place. The curtains of fine linen described above could be seen only by the priests from inside. Above that was the curtain of goats’ hair. Then over that were the coverings, an inner covering of rams’ skins dyed red and an outer covering of hides of fine leather. The movement is from the inside to the outside because it is God’s dwelling place; the approach of the worshiper would be the opposite. The pure linen represented the righteousness of God, guarded by the embroidered cherubim; the curtain of goats’ hair was a reminder of sin through the daily sin offering of a goat; the covering of rams’ skins dyed red was a reminder of the sacrifice and the priestly ministry set apart by blood, and the outer covering marked the separation between God and the world. These are the interpretations set forth by Kaiser; others vary, but not greatly (see W. C. Kaiser, Jr., “Exodus,” EBC 2:459).
This curtain will serve “for a tent over the tabernacle,” as a dwelling place.
Heb “you will make them”

verses.zh: 每幅幔子要长三十肘，宽四肘；十一幅幔子都要一样的尺寸。
verses.en: The length of each[NOTE:1] curtain is to be 45 feet, and the width of each curtain is to be 6 feet—the same size for the 11 curtains.
notes: Heb “one”

verses.zh: 要把五幅幔子连成一幅，又把六幅幔子连成一幅，这第六幅幔子要在罩棚的前面摺上去。
verses.en: You are to join five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves. You are to double over[NOTE:1] the sixth curtain at the front of the tent.
notes: The text seems to describe this part as being in front of the tabernacle, hanging down to form a valence at the entrance (S. R. Driver, Exodus, 284).

verses.zh: 在这相连的幔子末幅边上要做五十个钮扣；在那相连的幔子末幅边上也做五十个钮扣。
verses.en: You are to make 50 loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and 50 loops along the edge of the curtain that joins the second set.

verses.zh: 又要做五十个铜钩，钩在钮扣中，使罩棚连成一个。
verses.en: You are to make 50 bronze clasps and put the clasps into the loops and join the tent together so that it is a unit.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “one”

verses.zh: 罩棚的幔子所余那垂下来的半幅幔子，要垂在帐幕的后头。
verses.en: Now the part that remains of the curtains of the tent—the half curtain that remains will hang over at the back of the tabernacle.[NOTE:1]
notes: U. Cassuto (Exodus, 353) cites b. Shabbat 98b which says, “What did the tabernacle resemble? A woman walking on the street with her train trailing behind her.” In the expression “the half of the curtain that remains,” the verb agrees in gender with the genitive near it.

verses.zh: 罩棚的幔子所余长的，这边一肘，那边一肘，要垂在帐幕的两旁，遮盖帐幕。
verses.en: The foot and a half[NOTE:1] on the one side and the foot and a half on the other side of what remains in the length of the curtains of the tent will hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on one side and the other side, to cover it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Literally “cubit.”

U. Cassuto states the following: “To the north and to the south, since the tent curtains were 30 cubits long, there were 10 cubits left over on each side; these covered the 9 cubits of the curtains of the tabernacle and also the bottom cubit of the boards, which the tabernacle curtains did not suffice to cover. It is to this that v. 13 refers” (Exodus, 353).

verses.zh: 又要用染红的公羊皮做罩棚的盖；再用海狗皮做一层罩棚上的顶盖。
verses.en: “You are to make a covering[NOTE:1] for the tent out of ram skins dyed red and over that a covering of fine leather.[NOTE:2]
notes: Two outer coverings made of stronger materials will be put over the tent and the curtain, the two inner layers.
See the note on this phrase in Exod 25:5.

verses.zh: 「你要用皂荚木做帐幕的竖板。
verses.en: “You are to make the frames[NOTE:1] for the tabernacle out of[NOTE:2] acacia wood as uprights.[NOTE:3]
notes: There is debate whether the word הַקְּרָשִׁים (haqqerashim) means “boards” (KJV, ASV, NAB, NASB) or “frames” (NIV, NCV, NRSV, TEV) or “planks” (see Ezek 27:6) or “beams,” given the size of them. The literature on this includes M. Haran, “The Priestly Image of the Tabernacle,” HUCA 36 (1965): 192; B. A. Levine, “The Description of the Tabernacle Texts of the Pentateuch,” JAOS 85 (1965): 307-18; J. Morgenstern, “The Ark, the Ephod, and the Tent,” HUCA 17 (1942/43): 153-265; 18 (1943/44): 1-52.
“Wood” is an adverbial accusative.
The plural participle “standing” refers to how these items will be situated; they will be vertical rather than horizontal (U. Cassuto, Exodus, 354).

verses.zh: 每块要长十肘，宽一肘半；
verses.en: Each[NOTE:1] frame is to be 15 feet long, and each frame is to be 27 inches wide,
notes: Heb “the frame.”

verses.zh: 每块必有两榫相对。帐幕一切的板都要这样做。
verses.en: with two projections[NOTE:1] per frame parallel one to another.[NOTE:2] You are to make all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
notes: Heb “hands,” the reference is probably to projections that served as stays or supports. They may have been tenons, or pegs, projecting from the bottom of the frames to hold the frames in their sockets (S. R. Driver, Exodus, 286).
Or “being joined each to the other.”

verses.zh: 帐幕的南面要做板二十块。
verses.en: So you are to make the frames for the tabernacle: 20 frames for the south side,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “on the south side southward.”

verses.zh: 在这二十块板底下要做四十个带卯的银座，两卯接这块板上的两榫，两卯接那块板上的两榫。
verses.en: and you are to make 40 silver bases to go under the 20 frames—two bases under the first frame for its two projections, and likewise[NOTE:1] two bases under the next frame for its two projections;
notes: The clause is repeated to show the distributive sense; it literally says, “and two bases under the one frame for its two projections.”

verses.zh: 帐幕第二面，就是北面，也要做板二十块
verses.en: and for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, 20 frames,

verses.zh: 和带卯的银座四十个；这板底下有两卯，那板底下也有两卯。
verses.en: and their 40 silver bases, two bases under the first frame, and two bases under the next frame.

verses.zh: 帐幕的后面，就是西面，要做板六块。
verses.en: And for the back of the tabernacle on the west[NOTE:1] you will make six frames.
notes: Or “westward” (toward the sea).

verses.zh: 帐幕后面的拐角要做板两块。
verses.en: You are to make two frames for the corners[NOTE:1] of the tabernacle on the back.
notes: The term rendered “corners” is “an architectural term for some kind of special corner structure. Here it seems to involve two extra supports, one at each corner of the western wall” (N. M. Sarna, Exodus [JPSTC], 170).

verses.zh: 板的下半截要双的，上半截要整的，直顶到第一个环子；两块都要这样做两个拐角。
verses.en: At the two corners[NOTE:1] they must be doubled at the lower end and finished together at the top in one ring. So it will be for both.
notes: Heb “they will be for the two corners.” This is the last clause of the verse, moved forward for clarity.

verses.zh: 必有八块板和十六个带卯的银座；这板底下有两卯，那板底下也有两卯。
verses.en: So there are to be eight frames and their silver bases, sixteen bases, two bases under the first frame, and two bases under the next frame.

verses.zh: 「你要用皂荚木做闩：为帐幕这面的板做五闩，
verses.en: “You are to make bars of acacia wood, five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,

verses.zh: 为帐幕那面的板做五闩，又为帐幕后面的板做五闩。
verses.en: and five bars for the frames on the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames on the back of the tabernacle on the west.

verses.zh: 板腰间的中闩要从这一头通到那一头。
verses.en: The middle bar in the center of the frames will reach from end to end.[NOTE:1]
notes: These bars served as reinforcements to hold the upright frames together. The Hebrew term for these bars is also used of crossbars on gates (Judg 16:3; Neh 3:3).

verses.zh: 板要用金子包裹，又要做板上的金环套闩；闩也要用金子包裹。
verses.en: You are to overlay the frames with gold and make their rings of gold to provide places for the bars, and you are to overlay the bars with gold.

verses.zh: 要照着在山上指示你的样式立起帐幕。
verses.en: You are to set up the tabernacle according to the plan[NOTE:1] that you were shown on the mountain.
notes: The noun is מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat), often translated “judgment” or “decision” in other contexts. In those settings it may reflect its basic idea of custom, which here would be reflected with a rendering of “prescribed norm” or “plan.”

verses.zh: 「你要用蓝色、紫色、朱红色线，和捻的细麻织幔子，以巧匠的手工绣上基路伯。
verses.en: “You are to make a special curtain[NOTE:1] of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen; it is to be made[NOTE:2] with cherubim, the work of an artistic designer.
notes: Although translated “curtain” (traditionally “veil,” so ASV, NAB, NASB) this is a different word from the one used earlier of the tent curtains, so “special curtain” is used. The word פָּרֹכֶת (parokhet) seems to be connected with a verb that means “to shut off” and was used with a shrine. This curtain would form a barrier in the approach to God (see S. R. Driver, Exodus, 289).

The verb is the third masculine singular form, but no subject is expressed. It could be translated “one will make” or as a passive. The verb means “to make,” but probably has the sense of embroidering both here and in v. 1.

verses.zh: 要把幔子挂在四根包金的皂荚木柱子上，柱子上当有金钩，柱子安在四个带卯的银座上。
verses.en: You are to hang it[NOTE:1] with gold hooks[NOTE:2] on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold, set in[NOTE:3] four silver bases.
notes: Heb “put it.”
This clause simply says “and their hooks gold,” but is taken as a circumstantial clause telling how the veil will be hung.
Heb “on four silver bases.”

verses.zh: 要使幔子垂在钩子下，把法柜抬进幔子内；这幔子要将圣所和至圣所隔开。
verses.en: You are to hang this curtain under the clasps and bring the ark of the testimony in there behind the curtain.[NOTE:1] The curtain will make a division for you between the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place.[NOTE:2]
notes: The traditional expression is “within the veil,” literally “into the house (or area) of the (special) curtain.”
Or “the Holy of Holies.”

verses.zh: 又要把施恩座安在至圣所内的法柜上，
verses.en: You are to put the atonement lid on the ark of the testimony in the Most Holy Place.

verses.zh: 把桌子安在幔子外帐幕的北面；把灯台安在帐幕的南面，彼此相对。
verses.en: You are to put the table outside the curtain and the lampstand on the south side of the tabernacle, opposite the table, and you are to place the table on the north side.

verses.zh: 「你要拿蓝色、紫色、朱红色线，和捻的细麻，用绣花的手工织帐幕的门帘。
verses.en: “You are to make a hanging[NOTE:1] for the entrance of the tent of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.[NOTE:2]
notes: This was another curtain, serving as a screen in the entrance way. Since it was far away from the special curtain screening the Most Holy Place, it was less elaborate. It was not the work of the master designer, but of the “embroiderer,” and it did not have the cherubim on it.

The word רֹקֵם (roqem) refers to someone who made cloth with colors. It is not certain, however, whether the colors were woven into the fabric on the loom or applied with a needle; so “embroiderer” should be understood as an approximation (cf. HALOT 1290-91 s.v. רקם).

verses.zh: 要用皂荚木为帘子做五根柱子，用金子包裹。柱子上当有金钩；又要为柱子用铜铸造五个带卯的座。」
verses.en: You are to make for the hanging five posts of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and their hooks will be[NOTE:1] gold, and you are to cast five bronze bases for them.[NOTE:2]
notes: “will be” has been supplied.

In all the details of this chapter the expositor should pay attention to the overall message rather than engage in speculation concerning the symbolism of the details. It is, after all, the divine instruction for the preparation of the dwelling place for Yahweh. The point could be said this way: The dwelling place of Yahweh must be prepared in accordance with, and by the power of, his divine word. If God was to fellowship with his people, then the center of worship had to be made to his specifications, which were in harmony with his nature. Everything was functional for the approach to God through the ritual by divine provisions. But everything also reflected the nature of God, the symmetry, the order, the pure wood, the gold overlay, or (closer to God) the solid gold. And the symbolism of the light, the table, the veil, the cherubim—all of it was revelatory. All of it reflected the reality in heaven. Churches today do not retain the pattern and furnishings of the old tabernacle. However, they would do well to learn what God was requiring of Israel, so that their structures are planned in accordance with the theology of worship and the theology of access to God. Function is a big part, but symbolism and revelation instruct the planning of everything to be used. Christians live in the light of the fulfillment of Christ, and so they know the realities that the old foreshadowed. While a building is not necessary for worship (just as Israel worshiped in places other than the sanctuary), it is practical, and if there is going to be one, then the most should be made of it in the teaching and worshiping of the assembly. This chapter, then, provides an inspiration for believers on preparing a functional, symbolical, ordered place of worship that is in harmony with the word of God. And there is much to be said for making it as beautiful and uplifting as is possible—as a gift of freewill offering to God. Of course, the most important part of preparing a place of worship is the preparing of the heart. Worship, to be acceptable to God, must be in Christ. He said that when the temple was destroyed he would raise it up in three days. While he referred to his own body, he also alluded to the temple by the figure. When they put Jesus to death, they were destroying the temple; at his resurrection he would indeed begin a new form of worship. He is the tent, the curtain, the atonement, that the sanctuary foreshadowed. And then, believers also (when they receive Christ) become the temple of the Lord. So the NT will take the imagery and teaching of this chapter in a number of useful ways that call for more study. This does not, however, involve allegorization of the individual tabernacle parts.

commentary:
CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- I have chosen not to do a detailed verse-by-verse exegesis of these chapters. I am theologically wary of trying
to make the tabernacle applicable to the Christian life.

- This is interesting in understanding Israel's worship practices and procedures. The tabernacle was a physical
way to express the transcendence and immanence of God (see Outline V).

- Most of the details of the tabernacle are not meant to convey theological truth. Jesus is the new
tabernacle/temple (cf. John 2:19)! He, not Israel or her sacrificial system (cf. book of Hebrews), is the focus of NT revelation. God
used Israel to reveal Himself but now Jesus is the full and final revelation (i.e., Matt. 5:17-48; 12:3-6).
